escalation.lemma: Lemma 7.8 (five-colour proof, §7.4). Let B be an open disk containing a point m (the midpoint of an edge of a reduced closed graph word W in G = the geometric realisation of K_5), let g : B minus holes -> G be continuous and equal to q_eps outside all hole disks, and suppose a connected component C of g^{-1}(m) meets both the inner and outer boundary circles of an annulus A about a cyclic centre x. Then C contains a compact connected set crossing A from the inner to the outer boundary, disjoint from the holes, on which the edge labels of the reduced word are locally constant.
escalation.why_hard: The printed proof assumes g is defined on the whole annulus A; at a non-isolated cyclic centre every annulus meets further holes, so the annulus must first be made hole-free, which is what Theorem 6.5 (local finiteness of cyclic centres) supplies. The interface between Lemma 7.4's hole families, Theorem 6.5, and the annulus coordinates is exactly where this block stopped.
